children: The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia's SAR4.88 trillion ($1.26 trillion) pipeline of announced real estate and infrastructure projects is creating opportunities for the country's design and interior fit-out sectors, said top industry experts at the ongoing INDEX Saudi Arabia expo in Riyadh.

The leading interior design, furniture & fit-out trade event kicked off yesterday (September 15) bringing together designers, architects, developers and suppliers as the kingdom expands investment in its built environment and design industries.

The opening day saw top industry professionals discuss products and ideas that are helping shape the kingdom’s evolving design landscape, across sectors including furniture, lighting, surfaces, flooring, interior fit-out, textiles, décor, kitchen solutions and home automation, said the organisers, dmg events.

The three-day event, being held under the theme 'Built on heritage. Designed for tomorrow' will explore the role of cultural identity in contemporary Saudi design, from the materials and craftsmanship being used to the way new hospitality, residential and commercial spaces respond to their surroundings.

The theme will run across the event’s content and features, bringing Saudi and international perspectives together to examine how heritage, functionality and modern design are being interpreted across the Kingdom, said the organisers.

According to TechSci Research, the kingdom’s interior fit-out market is expected to reach SAR31.3 billion by 2031, thus reinforcing demand for the design, materials, furnishings and solutions needed to bring the Kingdom’s expanding pipeline of projects to life.

Elaine O’Connell, Senior Vice President – Design and Hospitality Division at dmg events, said: "INDEX Saudi Arabia brings together a design community that is increasingly confident in its own identity while remaining connected to ideas and innovation from around the world."

"What stands out this year is the strength of Saudi participation, from established industry leaders to emerging talent, alongside international brands bringing products, expertise and new perspectives to the Kingdom," she stated.
Next generation of Saudi design talent

A key feature of the 2026 edition is the INDEX Design Talks, where more than 60 architects, interior designers, fit-out specialists, developers, project owners and industry experts are taking part, with Saudi speakers accounting for more than half of the programme.

The programme will explore key themes shaping Saudi Arabia’s design sector, including “Designing Saudi Identity – Five Projects, Five Approaches,” “Inside the Client Mindset – What Clients Really Want from Design Teams,” and “Reality Check – How Do We Build the Next Generation of Designers?”

INDEX Saudi Arabia will also spotlight the next generation of Saudi design talent through INDEX Future Stars, which will see final-year interior design students from 11 Saudi universities present their projects to leading design professionals and compete for internship opportunities.

Returning for a second year, Trend Tours will offer visitors a curated journey across the show floor, highlighting key brands, products and emerging design trends. Developed in collaboration with industry partners CIOB and RIBA, the tours will provide expert-led insights into the innovations shaping the sector.

INDEX Saudi Arabia is co-located with Hotel & Hospitality Expo Saudi Arabia, thus bringing the interiors and hospitality value chains together and creating a complementary sourcing and networking platform for architects, designers, developers, hotel operators, procurement professionals, and contractors.
